title: Mayoral Candidate Cigarroa Listed as ‘No Response’ in City Drug-Testing Records; She Faults Budget Process at Debate
excerpt: City of Laredo records list mayoral candidate and District 8 Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa as “No Response” in the city’s voluntary drug-testing participation table, while at the October 14 mayoral debate at Texas A&M International University she criticized the city’s budgeting process and called for more community input.
content:
City of Laredo records list mayoral candidate and District 8 Councilmember Alyssa Cigarroa as “No Response” in the city’s voluntary drug-testing participation table.

The city’s published table, updated June 3, 2025, shows no opt-in or opt-out entry for Cigarroa, while most of her colleagues on the council show opt-in dates. Participation in the testing is voluntary, and the table records whether each elected official opted in, opted out, or did not respond.

Cigarroa is not the only official without an entry. The table also shows no opt-in or opt-out entry for District 2 Councilmember Ricardo “Richie” Rangel Jr. and District 3 Councilmember Melissa R. Cigarroa.

At the October 14, 2026, mayoral debate at Texas A&M International University, Cigarroa criticized the city’s budgeting process, saying the budget reaches the council incomplete and that the council should involve the community district by district and do a better job of staying within its means rather than raising the budget every year.

Her remarks also touched on the Plaza Theatre restoration project in her district, which has faced years of delays and questions about funding and its long-term sustainability. Webb Watch 956 has previously reported on the theatre’s restoration costs and delays.

Cigarroa led the November 3 mayoral field with 35.54 percent of the vote, ahead of Mayor Dr. Victor D. Treviño. Because no candidate won a majority, the race goes to a runoff. Early voting runs Monday, November 30, through Tuesday, December 8, and Election Day is Saturday, December 12.
